rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet says that if worldly beauty lasts, it lasts only one night, illustrating the mortality of earthly women's beauty, virginity, and youth.
rows.anchor: If it stays, it will stay for one night and not more

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raises the houris in a special way so their virginity, beauty, and youth never fade; each approach by a husband is like the first.
rows.anchor: their virginity, beauty and youth will never be lost

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ʿurub is a plural meaning a beloved and beautiful wife.
rows.anchor: It means “a beloved and beautiful wife.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although atrāb usually means women of the same age, Islahi prefers “bosom friends”; their equal age and friendship prevent preference, jealousy, or envy among the houris.
rows.anchor: in my opinion, here it means “women who are bosom friends.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The houris' husbands, like the houris, will remain youthful and graceful.
rows.anchor: their husbands too will remain young and graceful

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase for the companions of the right hand may attach to the previous verse, or serve as the predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: These words can relate to the previous verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first parsing, the houris raised with special attributes are for the companions of the right hand; on the second, all the blessings mentioned above are theirs.
rows.anchor: Almighty will be for the companions of the right hand

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi inclines to the first parsing; either reading preserves the basic purport, with only a subtle difference in eloquence.
rows.anchor: I am inclined to the first of these interpretations

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though most of the foremost believers belong to earlier generations and few later people join them, many from both early and later generations will form one group at resurrection.
rows.anchor: there will be one group from both the earlier and later generations

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The left-hand people suffer scorching winds, fire, and boiling water; after heat drives them toward water, they find only boiling water, as in 55:44.
rows.anchor: When after being agonized by the heat they will run towards water, they will only get boiling water to drink

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their smoky shade is black and supplies neither coolness nor protection or other benefit, echoing 77:31.
rows.anchor: this shade will neither be cool nor of any benefit

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their earlier affluence and luxury are not themselves crimes; rather, God's favors made gratitude and obedience incumbent, but they became arrogant and persisted in grave sin.
rows.anchor: it only mentions its severity. What is implied is that the Almighty had blessed them with comfort and affluence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reversal of status fulfills the sūrah's description of the Day as lowering some and elevating others: worldly high-status people fall into punishment.
rows.anchor: People who were at the top in this world have fallen into the deep pit of the Almighty’s punishment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “great sin” means polytheism, the greatest sin in religious philosophy and the greatest wrong according to the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: polytheism is the greatest sin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They denied resurrection and mocked the warning, asking how they and their long-dead forefathers could return after becoming dust and bones.
rows.anchor: they would make fun of it by asking how they and their forefathers who passed away a long time ago would be raised to life again

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must tell Quraysh that earlier and later peoples are being gathered by God until the appointed time, when all will be raised for judgment; the dead have not vanished from God.
rows.anchor: all of them are being assembled in the repository of God, and as soon as the time of reward and punishment comes, all of them will be raised

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition after lamajmūʿūn parallels the construction in 6:12, where God gathers people until Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: the way it is said in S ūrah An‘ ām

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh are directly addressed as astray deniers: because they practiced polytheism and denied the Hereafter, they will eat zaqqūm and drink scalding water like thirsty camels.
rows.anchor: they have gone astray from the path of monotheism and have also denied the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worldly wealth is set against zaqqūm as their afterlife food: they will eat its leaves and thorns, then drink boiling water.
rows.anchor: With reference to this, their fodder in the Hereafter will be of zaqqūm

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haym is the plural of ahyam, a camel suffering perpetual thirst that keeps drinking without its thirst being quenched.
rows.anchor: It refers to a camel who is afflicted with the malady of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuzul means the first food offered to a guest on arrival, so this dreadful first provision leaves one to imagine what they will eat later.
rows.anchor: refers to the edibles which are presented foremost to a guest as soon as he disembarks

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Section II answers the previously mentioned denial of resurrection and recompense with arguments, in a discourse whose rebuking tone and coherence are clear.
rows.anchor: The succeeding verses discuss the arguments about the Day of Judgement and the reward and punishment which will take place on that day

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address targets those denying Judgment, identified with the earlier speakers who questioned being raised after death.
rows.anchor: The address is directed to those who have denied

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings contribute only semen; God fashions it through the womb's dark stages into a healthy child and carries the person through every later stage of life, proving creation is God's work.
rows.anchor: Who takes it out from this womb in the form of a healthy child after making it pass through various stages in layers of darkness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death's net catches everyone, rich or poor and high or low, and God thereby gathers all people for Judgment; the theme returns in 83–87.
rows.anchor: Whether a person is of high or low status and whether he is rich or poor, he is bound to face death

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God controls life and death, He can replace people with similar beings and raise them in a world unknown to them.
rows.anchor: He has the power to create someone similar, and to raise man up in a world he knows not

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “we are not powerless” should be taken affirmatively to mean that God has power, as clarified by the way prepositions affect ellipsis and brevity.
rows.anchor: The meaning thus would be that God is not powerless; He is powerful

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For this wording and ellipsis, Islahi points to the parallel expression in 70:40–41.
rows.anchor: This topic is discussed in S ūrah al-Ma‘ārij thus

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nunshi'akum implies that God will create people under wholly different physical laws in an unknown world, then resurrect them, judge their deeds, and assign their eternal abode.
rows.anchor: God will create man in a world whose physical laws will be totally different, and he is totally unaware of them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their witnessed first creation should remind them that a second creation is possible; God's power and wisdom entail resurrection, since otherwise the world would be meaningless.
rows.anchor: A person does witness his creation in this world; why does he not learn the lesson from it that there is nothing improbable in being created again

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Crops are an unearned favor that grounds accountability; people often arrogantly ascribe such blessings to their own planning and ability and so ignore the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: they thought that they were a result of their own planning and ability and that they had a right to these favours

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People merely sow and plough; God gives the seed and earth the power to sprout, grow, flower, and ripen into what farmers need.
rows.anchor: it is God alone who supports these needles with stalks and causes the leaves to grow from them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can destroy a flourishing crop with wind or hail just when its owners celebrate success, exposing human helplessness.
rows.anchor: by sending a strong wind or a hailstorm, rout the blooming harvest at the very time people are expressing joy at this success

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word tuhūn is sarcastic: the ruined people are so bewildered that they cannot make sense of the loss or explain how others might help assess it.
rows.anchor: is used here sarcastically. The implied meaning is that people will become so unnerved

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited parable of the orchard owners portrays the crop-loss situation and their resulting ruin.
rows.anchor: which portrays this complete situation:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God turns bitter sea water into pure rain for people, livestock, and fields; attempts by scientists to make artificial rain are only child's play.
rows.anchor: converts the bitter water of the seas into water vapours and then once again rains it down on man in the form of pure, sweet and wholesome water

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God can turn bitter water sweet, He can also make drinkable water bitter and sour, rendering it useless.
rows.anchor: He can make this water so bitter and sour that it becomes useless for man

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The providential gifts of water require obedience and gratitude; otherwise people should expect punishment for ingratitude, a theme treated in al-Fātiḥah.
rows.anchor: all these favours require that man remain obedient to his Lord or else get ready to face punishment for his ungratefulness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude moves a person to take the first step toward God and is the sentiment he expresses on reaching his destination after his labor.
rows.anchor: It is this very sentiment which induces a person to take the first step towards his Lord

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For desert travelers without settlements, portable fire, or matches, God provided fire-producing stones and the markh and ʿafār trees, whose branches kindle fire when rubbed; Yā Sīn also mentions the tree.
rows.anchor: created certain types of stones which can be rubbed together to produce fire

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire and zaqqūm of Hell are real: as God combines fire and tree in the worldly markh and ʿafār, He can create zaqqūm in Hell; this answers Quraysh's mockery of 17:60.
rows.anchor: people who regard the union of fire and tree in Hell as impossible should learn a lesson from this tree in which God has combined both

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the close of the argument, the Prophet should hold his stance and glorify God despite stubborn rejecters, since the arguments support him.
rows.anchor: as far as the arguments are concerned, they are in his favour, yet these stubborn people are not budging to accept them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not create the world merely for people’s luxury or sport; He must bring a day rewarding gratitude and punishing ingratitude.
rows.anchor: It is incumbent upon Him to bring a day in which He rewards the grateful for their gratitude and takes to task the ingrates

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition bi in bi-ismi rabbika also expresses seeking help, so the Prophet glorifies God and asks His aid against these circumstances.
rows.anchor: shows that the word here also embraces the meaning of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Name signifies that God's noble attributes are the means of knowing and relating to Him, the source of true knowledge and deeds.
rows.anchor: the only means of a person’s association and relationship with the Almighty are His noble attributes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Section III closes the sūrah by affirming the Qur'an's reality and divine, protected transmission, calling it guidance and spiritual food, and warning Quraysh that rejecting it cannot save them from God's coming judgment.
rows.anchor: The leaders of the Quraysh are addressed and told that the certain event the Qur’ ān is informing them of is a reality

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle lā is separate from uqsimu; before the oath's affirmation, it negates the addressee's false view, a familiar Arabic and Qur'anic usage.
rows.anchor: Before the affirmation, the particle serves to negate the wrong view of the addressee

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi illustrates the construction with 4:65: verbal profession alone does not make hypocrites true believers, who must accept the Prophet's arbitration.
